title: Sort the stack
source_of_copy: claude/sessions_industry-acumen-master.md, Part 3, practice 6 (slides 44 and 45). Edit there first, then regenerate this file. Versions 2.1 to 3.0 were edited in the portal (hgm-doc) on 6 Oct 2026: 2.2 gives every card the boxes the tools training lists for its vendor; 3.0 makes each box a pool the game draws per_box cards from, and round 3 a pool it draws per_run suites from, so no two runs are the same (vendor-icons.json 1.3). Bring the master in line with it before regenerating.
made_up_line: The vendor names are real; every property and owner in this session is made up.
finish: That's the stack. Hear the name, place it in a box, ask what it's for.

boxes.name: PMS
boxes.job: Where every reservation lives and the front desk checks guests in

boxes.name: Channel manager
boxes.job: Sends rates and availability to the OTAs so a room isn't sold twice

boxes.name: Booking engine
boxes.job: The "Book now" page on the property's own website

boxes.name: Dynamic pricing
boxes.job: Moves nightly prices up and down with demand

cards.note: Mews' main product is its PMS. It now sells most of the stack itself: booking engine, upsells, revenue management (it bought Atomize in 2024), a channel manager powered by SiteMinder (May 2026) and guest messaging (October 2026). CRM still comes from partners.
The PMS Hyatt chose for its hotels worldwide, and one IHG approves. Oracle also sells it a channel manager (OPERA Cloud Distribution) and upsells (Nor1) as add-ons.
From the campground and holiday-park world, where many glamping stacks start. Its own channel manager, booking engine, pricing rules, guest inbox, email campaigns and pre-arrival offers are built in.

A PMS for hotels, holiday parks and campgrounds, now branded RMS. Its own channel manager, booking engine, rule-based pricing, guest chat and a guest portal that sells extras come with it, and email campaigns are a paid module. Careful: in hotel tech "RMS" usually means revenue management; this one is a PMS.
SiteMinder's all-in-one for small properties: PMS, channel manager and booking engine in every plan, competitor rates on the Pro plan, and pricing, guest messaging and upsells as paid add-ons.
Vacation-rental software, a PMS first, with a channel manager, a booking website, one inbox for guest messages and upsells in its guest portal. Its dynamic pricing costs extra.

Known for its channel manager; it also sells a booking engine and competitor-rate insights, with pricing (Dynamic Revenue Plus) and guest messaging and upsells (Guest Engagement) as paid add-ons. Its PMS for small properties is a separate product, Little Hotelier.
A channel manager for independents, hotel groups and vacation rentals; it also sells its own booking engine, pricing tools and a competitor rate checker (RateSTalk).
Connects hotels to 500+ OTAs and other channels: chains through their reservation system, independents through Property Connector.
Sells rate-intelligence tools for hotels; it also sells a channel manager and a booking engine (UNO).

Vacation-rental software: PMS and channel manager in every plan, pushing listings to Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com, with a booking engine, a CRM and one guest inbox. Pricing and guest-app upsells are paid add-ons.
Sells all eight jobs: the PMS, channel manager, booking engine, upsells and guest messaging in its plans, and pricing, rate shopping and a CRM as paid add-ons. Ask which parts they use.
The booking engine on the SynXis central reservation system, which also sends rates and availability to the OTAs as a channel manager. Sabre sold SynXis in 2025; Aven Hospitality sells it now.
Amadeus' booking engine for hotels and resorts; it also sells a channel manager as a paid add-on.

Vacation-rental software (a PMS): syncs Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com, runs the property's own booking website and puts guest messages in one inbox. Its top plans add dynamic pricing (powered by Beyond).
A cloud PMS for independent hotels, lodges and inns, with its own commission-free booking engine; guests can add extras before arrival in its guest portal. OTA connections come through partners.
Vacation-rental pricing, formerly Beyond Pricing, with market data in every plan. It also sells Signal, a direct-booking website and engine, as a paid add-on.
Grew up in short-term rentals. It also shows what nearby listings charge, night by night.
Same world as Wheelhouse, now sold to hotels too. Market data and rate shopping come with it.
A hotel revenue-management system: the bigger-hotel end of this box.
A hotel revenue-management system, and IDeaS' main rival at resorts and groups. Its channel manager, rate shopping, CRM and upsells all come from partners.
Automated pricing for smaller hotels, B&Bs and inns. It watches competitors only to set its own prices, so it isn't a rate shopper.
Automated hotel pricing, bought by Mews in 2024 and now sold as Mews RMS.

rounds.title: Around the guest and the market

boxes.name: Rate shopping and market intelligence
boxes.job: Shows what nearby properties charge, and how the market is doing

boxes.name: CRM
boxes.job: Holds past guests' stays and spend, so you can market to them

boxes.name: Guest messaging
boxes.job: Texts and chats with guests before and during the stay

boxes.name: Upsell
boxes.job: Sells upgrades and extras before and at arrival

cards.note: Formerly OTA Insight, so owners may still use the old name. It now also sells automated pricing and, for small independents, a channel manager and a booking engine.
Market data for vacation rentals: what the area's rentals charge and earn. Since September 2026 it also sells dynamic pricing (Adapt).
Market data for short-term and vacation rentals, built from managers' own data: what comparable rentals charge and book. It isn't a pricing tool.
Benchmarking for hotels: how occupancy, ADR and RevPAR compare with an anonymous comp set. It reports aggregated data only, never one competitor's price.
Forward-looking market data: what's already on the books in the market for future dates. Amadeus' booking engine is a different product, iHotelier.
Guest data and email marketing for hotels, including pre-arrival upgrade offers by email; it also sells guest chat as a separate product.
A hotel CRM; it also sells a booking engine, a central reservation system that sends rates to the OTAs, and revenue management (Guestrev).
HGM's own CRM: where the leads and the email list our funnel builds live, with texting and chat built in. The property's hotel CRM is a second list.
A general CRM some owners run, usually for sales enquiries such as weddings and groups rather than past guests.
The email tool a small owner often calls their CRM: a list and campaigns, not guest history.
Email and SMS marketing with more automation than Mailchimp; it can pull stays in from a PMS such as Cloudbeds.
A guest communication hub that sells upsells too.
Guest messaging for hotels, with upsells built in.
Now part of Cloudbeds, sold as Cloudbeds Guest Experience: guest messaging plus an upsell store.
Texts with guests and answers most messages itself. It also sells upsells in every plan and a CRM as a paid module.
A guest experience platform for vacation rentals and boutique stays: one inbox for every channel, upsells, and guest profiles to segment and market to.
Hotel guest messaging by text, now sold as Kipsu Engage FCX.
Now owned by Plusgrade, still sold as Oaky.
Oracle's hotel upsell product; pairs with OPERA.
Hotel upsells, including guests bidding for an upgrade.
The group that bought Oaky in 2025: room-upgrade bidding, early check-in, late checkout and extras for hotels, after starting with airline upgrades.

rounds.title: One suite, many jobs
rounds.intro: Now the other way round. Here's a suite. Drag in only the jobs it does.

suites.note: Sells all eight: the PMS, channel manager, booking engine, upsells and guest messaging in its plans, and pricing, rate shopping and a CRM as paid add-ons. So "we're on Cloudbeds" still doesn't tell you what they use it for. Ask.

A channel manager that also sells a booking engine and competitor-rate insights, with paid add-ons for pricing (Dynamic Revenue Plus) and for guest messaging and upsells (Guest Engagement). Its PMS for small properties is a separate product, Little Hotelier.

Mews' main product is its PMS. It now sells most of the stack itself: booking engine, upsells, revenue management (it bought Atomize in 2024), a channel manager powered by SiteMinder (May 2026) and guest messaging (October 2026). CRM still comes from partners.

SiteMinder's all-in-one for small properties: PMS, channel manager and booking engine in every plan, competitor rates on the Pro plan, and pricing, guest messaging and upsells as paid add-ons. A CRM comes only through other companies' apps.
From the campground world: PMS, channel manager, booking engine, pricing rules, a guest inbox, email campaigns and pre-arrival offers, all built in. It has no rate shopper of its own.
A hotel CRM with guest chat and pre-arrival upgrade emails. It sells no PMS, channel manager, booking engine, pricing tool or rate shopper: it connects to those.
